description: Measure sounds in Live: the tracks heard side by side in one pass (8 bars from from_beat unless beats says). Each sound gets its attack, decay (and how it sits against a beat), sustain, brightness, noisiness, pitch drop (an 808's or a kick's), modulation rate (and the beats a cycle), warmth (2nd and 3rd harmonics, even against odd), width, top (bandwidth), noise floor, tail (a dry hit falls far, a reverberant one hangs on) and crackle, and its effects: its decay time (RT60, said as a reverb when its tails fall in two slopes, the second slower) and how its tails darken and widen, echoes (their time as a note value, repeats, how far each falls and darkens), how deep its level swings, how far its brightness moves (a filter sweeping; a bass line's read against its notes) and how often, pumping against the beat, and its tail's share bar by bar. Plus its problems: clicks at note edges, DC, a note jumping out, tails cut off, echoes out of time, repeats that don't die away, an effect's tail burying the dry hits. Several tracks are judged as a kit too: a piece whose noise floor, top or grit sits apart from pieces of a similar range, pieces piling up or a wide gap between them, a piece ringing into its own next hit, and pieces that sound the same. With against (a kick, say), how far each track ducks under it and how fast it comes back, and whether their hits interlock or collide. With key, how far a low part's notes (its bass line) sit from it. To move a sound toward a reference sound, judge it with goal.sound.

tracks.description: The tracks to measure (names or refs)

against.description: A track the others duck under or play against (its name or ref)

key.description: The song's key, like "F# minor", "Bb major" or "D dorian"

from_beat.description: Where to listen from, in beats

beats.description: How long, in beats (8 bars when left out)
